agree.reason: The letter is polite and the market point is strong, but a landlord who still raises the 2024 late payments and has a coffee chain asking about the space gets no reason to trust this tenant over the chain, and no deadline or quick-signing commitment to act on.

honest.reason: All the figures check out ($26/sq ft, about $5,740 by year five, 18%), and 'a rate the market hasn't yet accepted' is a fair reading of a 14-month vacancy, though 'no vacancy or turnover costs' is stated more absolutely than the facts support.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter correctly works out the per-square-foot rate and the year-five rent, but it never puts a cost on vacancy (14 months empty at his rate is about $79,000 lost), never points out that year five goes above his $5,650 ask, and doesn't use the roughly $40,000 a new tenant would pay for a hood.

right_comparison.reason: It contrasts the offer with a unit listed for 14 months at $28, which is the right alternative, but it doesn't spell out what choosing the coffee chain or an empty space would actually cost him in lost rent and build-out.

qualification.reason: The letter makes a firm offer with no hedges that need conditions, so a qualification score doesn't apply.

objections.reason: It says nothing about the late payments he still brings up, though the facts answer that objection directly (the cooler failure, on-time payment ever since, automatic payment offered), and it treats the coffee chain only with a vague courtesy.

fit.reason: It is short, polite and under 300 words as asked, but it leaves placeholders for names the user knew (Frank Halloran, Pho Lan) and has no response date before June 1.
